**Finding submitted: deviation (critical, IP — ownership of deliverables).**

- **Where:** § 13.5 Ownership (p0115–p0116).
- **Issue:** The clause correctly gives Corio ownership of Developments it creates solely (and includes a Commerce One assignment of any residual claim), but the carve-out — "*unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights*" — transfers our own work product to the Vendor with no licence back. That fails even the fallback (which requires at least a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence) and sits in walk-away territory.
- **Not flagged:** § 2.8 (Commerce One retains the Software) is acceptable vendor-platform ownership; § 6 trademark rights are mutual; the "to be negotiated" sentence on Software enhancements and the absence of a Customer Data ownership sentence are noted as sub-elements only.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** delete the ownership carve-out so Corio owns all Developments, with a comment offering a licence to Commerce One for Developments it maintains as the fallback.
